findings.text: The test pins only part of the export contract. It rejects a case-changing id, but a trimming implementation and one that debug-logs the token both still pass. T-1 'verbatim' is therefore witnessed for only one input shape, and T-2 is not witnessed at all. The shipped code satisfies both rules (no logging, id returned unchanged), so this does not block. A later change to this function could break either rule with the test staying green.

debt.drag: Future edits to vesselExport can break T-1 for whitespace ids, or T-2, without any test failing.

findings.text: The journey lane behind I-1's witness (test id 'export') does not run vesselExport. Its argv is jsonl-lane.sh, which runs a test fake that reports the outcome scripted in witness-control.json ('*' tree, export: pass). The 'missing: none / failing: none' witness check and the arc-journey pass therefore say nothing about this code, and would report the same on any tree. I did not count them as evidence for I-1. My I-1 grade rests on the unit lane's 'export record shape' test, reading the code and my direct run. The lane is plan-side and outside this diff, so the builder cannot fix it. If the root wants a real witness for I-1, the plan has to change.

debt.drag: The obligation ledger can show I-1 as witnessed by a lane that never executes the export.

reasons: A1 met: packages/wheat/src/vessel-export.ts adds vesselExport, which accepts { id, token } and returns { vessel: id }, and the test sits in packages/wheat/test/. T-1 holds: a direct run returned 'Oak-7', ' a b ', 'ÄÖ', '' and '0007' unchanged. T-2 holds: the function does not log and does not return the token. It is pure, so it does not conflict with contracts/api.md.

A2 met: regenerating with node tools/gen-goldens.ts in a clean export of HEAD gave goldens identical to the commit (diff -rq, 'goldens-same'), which matches the executor's check. A semantic comparison shows goldens/wheat.json changes only by the new vessel-export module entry; every other module is identical. No other golden or source file changed.
Non-goals respected: the diff is exactly the three expected files.
I-1 is met on the unit lane test and my direct run, not on the journey witness, which is scripted (see note). The unit lane passed 51/51 and includes 'export record shape'.
Ruling C-1 is cited in the spec but appears in no corpus rule, and I did not read the rulings ledger, as instructed. This verdict makes no claim about C-1 beyond the cited contract and T-1/T-2.
The two notes are non-blocking: the shipped behaviour is correct, and the gaps are in test strength and a plan-side lane.

premises.claim: vesselExport returns the caller's id unchanged in the vessel field, drops the token and does no logging.
T-1 and T-2 are the export contract rules that apply; T-3 to T-42 concern the archived tariff screen.
Goldens are written only by the generator, which lists each module's exported signatures, so adding a module inserts one entry.
